data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.spec_note: mass/power fields are taken from the first sentence in the NASA description that states a mass in kg or a power in W; they may describe a sub-unit or a mode. Read the sentence.
record.name: Long Range Reconnaissance Imager (LORRI)
record.mission_name: New Horizons Pluto Kuiper Belt Flyby
record.description: The New Horizons Long Range Reconnaissance Imager (LORRI) is a panchromatic narrow angle imager. The primary objectives of the experiment are to obtain long range coverage of the Pluto Charon system for advance planning for the flyby, obtain images at 40 km resolution or better of the entire surface of Pluto for 3.2 days preceding and following the encounter, and return close-up images of the surface of Pluto during the closest approach. LORRI is mounted on the side of the spacecraft opposite the RTG. It consists of a 20.8 cm aperture telescope which focuses visible light on a 1024 x 1024 pixel CCD. There are no filters or moving parts. The instrument has a 5.06 x 5.06 milliradian field of view with a resolution of 0.00494 milliradians/pixel. This will give roughly 100 meter resolution during closest approach, depending on the final flyby distance selected. The wavelength range covered is 350 - 850 nm.
